To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the most important sources of residential and neighborhood satisfaction are the physical and social qualities of the neighborhood and the house itself, that these objective qualities of the neighborhood are more important than subjective evaluations, and that the subjective evaluations of the neighborhood are themselves largely influenced by the objective qualities of the residential environment and not by the subjective evaluations of neighbors.

residential and community satisfaction are primarily determined by the quality of the residential environment, and that this quality is largely a function of housing and neighborhood conditions that are determined primarily by the social class and racial/ethnic status of the residents.
residential satisfaction is a function of the degree of fit between the objective features of one’s housing and neighborhood and the subjective preferences and needs of residents.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the social psychology of residential experience and the social and psychological consequences of residential environments.
the social and psychological consequences of the residential environment and the social organization of communities.
the relationship between social and community characteristics of the residential environment and the satisfaction of residents with their housing and community.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the quality of the physical environment is the most important single source of residential and community attachment.
the residential environment is a primary determinant of residential satisfaction.
objective features of the physical environment, and the social class or minority group status of the household, are the most important determinants of residential and community attachment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the residential environment has an important impact on the quality of life, but that this impact is primarily through the effects of the residential environment on the individual's sense of well-being and satisfaction with his or her residential situation.
residential satisfaction is a function of residential quality, which is in turn a function of social class and majority/minority group status.
residential attachment is a complex function of the objective and subjective aspects of the residential environment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
residential and community satisfaction are strongly related to the objective quality of the residential environment.
residential satisfaction is a function of the quality of the physical environment, and not of social integration.
the residential environment is a significant factor in determining residential satisfaction.
